decisions.decision: Rollback uses the version-1 file with optional due fields that 1.4.0 strips on its next save, so operators are expected to keep a due-bearing copy and protect ticket changes made during rollback when upgrading again.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected original due times and all ticket changes to survive a writable rollback and re-upgrade automatically.

decisions.decision: The specification assigns and saves due times for new tickets even while DUE_TIMES is off, with the flag controlling what the HTTP API exposes.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant for tickets created while the flag is off to receive their first due time during backfill, under the policy and priority in effect then.

decisions.decision: Due times use continuous elapsed hours, including nights, weekends and holidays.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant for the promised hours to count only while the help desk is open.

decisions.decision: The overdue filter narrows the results of the current status-or-priority matching rule, so a ticket that is overdue can match just one of those two parameters.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a combined query to require the ticket to match overdue, status and priority together, as the existing API documentation describes for its filters.

decisions.decision: Unset SLA hour overrides use the stated defaults, while an invalid override is treated as a configuration error that identifies the offending variable.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have preferred the service to start with the default for that priority and warn the operator about the invalid override.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:7 (R-1, unset and invalid values); repo/src/config.js:21 (existing configuration error convention)

decisions.decision: The delivery is a local handoff with rollout instructions and fixture-based verification, with production rollout left to operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected an operator-assisted rehearsal with a copy of the production data before accepting the release.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md:173 (delivery summary); record/04-spec.md:51 (verification and production authority); repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md:20 (available access)

decisions.decision: Backfill adds due times without changing ticket update timestamps, adding audit entries or queuing notifications.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted backfilled due times to appear in the ticket history so operators could see when they were assigned.

decisions.decision: The enabled HTTP ticket responses expose due times, while the existing CLI table, ticket details and raw report output keep their current fields.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have meant for operators to see due times in the human-readable CLI list and ticket details while preserving the script-facing raw output.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:11 (R-2), :23 (R-5), and :27 (CLI contracts); repo/src/format.js:12, :22, and :47 (current output fields)

decisions.decision: The overdue list retains ticket ID order and the existing cursor pagination.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the most overdue tickets to appear first, with pagination following due-time order.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:11 (R-2, sort and cursor); repo/docs/api.md:79 (existing order)

decisions.decision: The API represents due as an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC, following the convention for its other timestamps.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected a numeric Unix timestamp for direct comparison in consuming systems.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md:11 (R-2, ISO due); repo/docs/api.md:10 (UTC timestamp convention)
